IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
BOINI MAHIPAL AND ANOTHER v. THE STATE OF TELANGANA
Citation: 2023 INSC 627 | Criminal Appeal No. 1750 of 2023
Bench: Division Bench of the Supreme Court of India
Date of Judgment: July 19, 2023
JUDGMENT & LEGAL PRINCIPLES
This criminal appeal challenges the judgment and order passed by the High Court regarding the conviction of
the appellants under Section 323 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), following their acquittal
on the primary charge of murder under Section 302 IPC.
FACTUAL BACKGROUND & TRIAL PROCEEDINGS
The appellants (Accused Nos. 3 and 4) were charged alongside others in connection with an incident resulting
in fatal injuries to the deceased. The Trial Court evaluated the eye-witness testimony and medical evidence,
concluding that while shared intention to cause murder under Section 302 IPC was not established beyond
reasonable doubt, voluntary causing hurt under Section 323/34 IPC was proved.
RATIO DECIDENDI & COURT FINDINGS
1. Appreciation of Evidence in Criminal Appeals: The Supreme Court re-evaluated the testimony of prosecution
witnesses and highlighted the necessity of maintaining consistency between medical testimony and ocular
evidence.
2. Application of Section 34 IPC (Common Intention): The Court examined whether common intention could be
inferred merely from presence at the scene or required active participation in the specific overt act.
3. Standard of Proof: Reaffirming established principles, the Court reiterated that where two views are
reasonably possible from the evidence, the benefit of doubt must accrue to the accused.
ORDER & DISPOSITION
The Supreme Court disposed of the appeal, modifying the sentence and upholding the legal standards
governing common intention and evidentiary appreciation in criminal trials.
